info.title: Reckon One API v2
info.description: Manage accounting data in Reckon One books, including customers, suppliers, invoices, bills, banking, payroll and superannuation records.

get.summary: Gets a list of address types.
get.description:
See [here](https://help.reckon.com/category/t3ohcrldj7) for details of filtering, sorting and selecting.

---

get.summary: Gets a list of financial institutions.
get.description:
See [here](https://help.reckon.com/category/t3ohcrldj7) for details of filtering, sorting and selecting.
            
---
            
Get a list of financial institutions.
            
`GET /5af6572c-9771-4b86-995d-3374d3bc683c/banking/financialinstitutions`
            
---
            
Get a specific page of financial institutions. Find out more about [paging](https://help.reckon.com/article/6dwfu9hgta-reckon-one-api-v2-paging).
            
`GET /5af6572c-9771-4b86-995d-3374d3bc683c/banking/financialinstitutions?page=2&perpage=20`
            
---
            
Get just the required fields, e.g. id and name. Find out more about [selecting](https://help.reckon.com/article/h9sxz6smwn-reckon-one-api-v2-selecting).
            
`GET /5af6572c-9771-4b86-995d-3374d3bc683c/banking/financialinstitutions?select=id,name`
            
---
            
Filter the results to return just the financial institutions that you want. Find out more about [filtering](https://help.reckon.com/article/ksqce865me-reckon-one-api-v2-filtering).
            
`GET /5af6572c-9771-4b86-995d-3374d3bc683c/banking/financialinstitutions?filter=name in ('Bank A','Bank B')`
            
---
            
Get in the required order, e.g. by name. Find out more about [sorting](https://help.reckon.com/article/e0iok3ydto-reckon-one-api-v2-sorting).
            
`GET /5af6572c-9771-4b86-995d-3374d3bc683c/banking/financialinstitutions?orderby=name`

parameters.name: perPage
parameters.description: The number of financial institutions per page.

404.description: The specified book does not exist.

401.description: The authentication token is missing, expired or invalid.

---

### Bank accounts
When creating a bank account, you can provide additional details via the `bankAccount` field. You must **omit** the `parentLedgerAccount` and `defaultTaxRate` fields.

### Credit account
When creating a credit account (for a credit card for example), you can provide additional details via the `creditAccount` field. You must **omit** the `parentLedgerAccount` and `defaultTaxRate` fields.

### Any other account
When creating any other account, you must **omit** the `bankAccount` and `creditAccount` fields.

post.summary: Creates a new recurring transaction template.
post.description:
Create a new recurring transaction template of any of five types - bill, invoice, journal,
payment or receipt - selected by `transactionType`. `template`'s shape depends on
`transactionType`:
            
- `Bill` - supplierId, amountTaxStatus, lineItems (each with either accountDetails or itemDetails), classificationId, templateId, reference, notes, billDiscountAmount, billDiscountPercent
- `Invoice` - customerId, amountTaxStatus, lineItems, classificationId, templateId, paymentTermsId, reference, notes, paymentDetails, invoiceDiscountAmount, invoiceDiscountPercent, purchaseOrderNumber, customFields
- `Journal` - summary, amountTaxStatus, description, adjustingJournal, lineItems (each with ledgerAccountId and exactly one of debit or credit)
- `Payment` - supplierId, bankAccountId, paymentMethodId, classificationId, reference, notes, internalNotes, lineItems
- `Receipt` - customerId, bankAccountId, paymentMethodId, classificationId, reference, notes, internalNotes, lineItems
            
`POST /5af6572c-9771-4b86-995d-3374d3bc683c/recurringtransactions`

requestBody.description: Details of the recurring transaction to create.

201.description: The id of the recurring transaction template that has been created.

400.description: The recurring transaction could not be created as the request contains invalid data.

404.description: The specified book does not exist.

403.description: The user does not have permission to create recurring transactions, or the transaction type is not enabled for this book.

401.description: The authentication token is missing, expired or invalid.

get.summary: Gets a list of recurring transaction templates.
get.description:
Get a paged list of the book's active and inactive recurring transaction templates, generic
across all transaction types. Deleted templates are never returned.
            
`GET /5af6572c-9771-4b86-995d-3374d3bc683c/recurringtransactions`
            
---
            
Get a specific page. Find out more about [paging](https://help.reckon.com/article/6dwfu9hgta-reckon-one-api-v2-paging).
            
`GET /5af6572c-9771-4b86-995d-3374d3bc683c/recurringtransactions?page=2&perpage=20`
            
---
            
Filter the results to return just the recurring transactions you want. Find out more about [filtering](https://help.reckon.com/article/ksqce865me-reckon-one-api-v2-filtering).
Every field except `frequency` can be filtered; `contains`, `startswith` and `endswith` apply to
`name`, `contactName` and `reference` only. To combine `or` with `and`, put the `or` conditions in
parentheses. Unscheduled templates have no next occurrence, so a `nextTransactionDate` condition
excludes them.
            
`GET /5af6572c-9771-4b86-995d-3374d3bc683c/recurringtransactions?filter=nextTransactionDate ge '2026-10-01' and nextTransactionDate le '2026-10-31'`
            
`GET /5af6572c-9771-4b86-995d-3374d3bc683c/recurringtransactions?filter=status eq 'active' and recurringType eq 'scheduled'`
            
Filter by several statuses, transaction types or contacts with `anyof`. `contactId` can be filtered
with `eq` or `anyof` only.
            
`GET /5af6572c-9771-4b86-995d-3374d3bc683c/recurringtransactions?filter=transactionType anyof ('invoice','bill') and contactId anyof ('b581a643-10dd-4d09-9a63-356654339795','8c5a1f0e-2f5d-4c5e-9d68-8a8f2f4c6d11')`
            
Search several fields at once.
            
`GET /5af6572c-9771-4b86-995d-3374d3bc683c/recurringtransactions?filter=status eq 'active' and (name contains "rent" or contactName contains "rent" or reference contains "rent")`
            
---
            
Sort in the required order, e.g. by next occurrence and then by name. Find out more about [sorting](https://help.reckon.com/article/e0iok3ydto-reckon-one-api-v2-sorting).
            
`GET /5af6572c-9771-4b86-995d-3374d3bc683c/recurringtransactions?orderby=nextTransactionDate,name desc`

parameters.name: perPage
parameters.description: The number of recurring transactions per page.

Actions are grouped into the sections they are presented under, and `actionCount` is how many are
available across all of them. An action the book's plan or feature flags exclude is absent from the
response rather than present and unavailable.
---

parameters.description: The kind of transaction the actions are being resolved for.

404.description: The specified book does not exist.

403.description: The user does not have permission to retrieve the transaction actions.

401.description: The authentication token is missing, expired or invalid.

get.summary: Gets what one transaction action has to offer for a contact.
get.description:
The action type carries the transaction type it belongs to, so no `transactionType` is needed here.
Each action has its own payload shape; `rowType`, `itemTypes`, `search`, `orderby`, `page` and
`perPage` apply to the actions that present a list and are ignored by the rest. `total` counts what
the filter matched and `unfilteredTotal` counts what the contact has at all, so an empty book and a
search that matched nothing can be told apart from one response.
            
`itemTypes` may be repeated to keep several. A ledger account has no item type, so asking for any
item type returns items only.
            
`InvoiceFrequentlyUsed` can be ordered by `name`, `code`, `itemType`, `description`, `unitPrice`,
`accountName`, `taxGroupName`, `rowType`, `usageCount` and `lastUsedDate`. Any other field is
ignored and the rows come back in the action's own ranking of most used, then most recently used.
            
`InvoiceRecentTransactions` returns whole transactions, newest first, each carrying the lines
that can be copied — so `perPage` counts transactions, not lines, and defaults to 5. It can be
ordered by `date` and `transactionNumber`; any other field is ignored. `rowType` does not apply and
is ignored. `itemTypes` filters the lines within each transaction, and a transaction left with no
lines drops from the page and from both totals. `search` matches a transaction's number or any of
its line descriptions, and a matched transaction comes back with all of its lines.
---
`GET /5af6572c-8b6b-4b0c-9a3f-0b5b7f5a1d2e/transactionActions/InvoiceFrequentlyUsed/details?contactId=3f2504e0-4f89-11d3-9a0c-0305e82c3301&rowType=Item&itemTypes=Product&itemTypes=Inventory&search=consulting&orderby=name asc&page=1&perPage=10`
            
`GET /5af6572c-8b6b-4b0c-9a3f-0b5b7f5a1d2e/transactionActions/InvoiceRecentTransactions/details?contactId=3f2504e0-4f89-11d3-9a0c-0305e82c3301&page=1&perPage=5`

parameters.name: rowType
parameters.description: The row type to keep, or omitted for all of them.

parameters.name: itemTypes
parameters.description: The item types to keep, or omitted for all of them.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Text to match rows against, or omitted to match everything.

parameters.name: orderby
parameters.description: How to order the rows, as comma separated `field direction` clauses, or omitted for the action's own ranking.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: The page to return, counting from one.

parameters.name: perPage
parameters.description: How many rows the page holds, or omitted for the action's own default.

200.description:
The details of the `InvoiceFrequentlyUsed` action.
or

`GET /e7e3ba02-05e2-4bea-9348-85876c9952ba/users?filter=employee.name eq "Joe Bloggs"`

CreateRecurringTransactionRequest.description:
A recurring transaction to create over REST. One endpoint accepts all five recurring
transaction types; Template's shape depends on TransactionType
and is resolved by the helper rather than by model binding.

schedule.description:
The schedule that determines when each occurrence is generated. Required unless
RecurringScheduleType is Unscheduled, in which case it is optional and,
when supplied, only its timing fields are used to compute reminders.

recurringScheduleType.description: The type of schedule for the recurring transaction. Defaults to Scheduled.

transactionType.description:
The type of transaction this template generates. Determines how Template
is interpreted.

autoSendEmail.description:
Whether each generated transaction should be automatically emailed. Only applies to
Bill and Invoice; ignored for Journal, Payment and Receipt.

sendDate.description: The date to send the email on, when AutoSendEmail is true. Only applies to Bill.

template.description:
The transaction-type-specific template. Its shape is one of five concrete types
(bill, invoice, journal, payment or receipt), selected by TransactionType.

RecurringScheduleInput.description: The schedule of a recurring transaction. Common to all recurring transaction types.

frequency.description: How often the recurring schedule repeats.

startDate.description: The date and time that the recurring schedule starts.

endCondition.description: The condition that ends the recurring schedule.

RecurringFrequencyInput.description: The frequency of a recurring schedule. Common to all recurring transaction types.

value.description: The number of frequency periods between each occurrence.

lastDayOfEachMonth.description: Whether the transaction recurs on the last day of each month.

FrequencyPeriod.description: Frequency period for a recurring template.

RecurringEndConditionInput.description: The end condition of a recurring schedule. Common to all recurring transaction types.

value.description: The end value, interpreted based on the type: null for "Never", a number of occurrences for "After", or a date for "AtDate".

FrequencyEndType.description: Frequency end type for a recurring template.

RecurringTransOptionsInput.description: Options for a recurring transaction. Common to all recurring transaction types.

autoPaymentProvider.description: The provider used to automatically take payment for the recurring transaction.

RecurringTransactionType.description: The type of a recurring transaction. The values match the domain recurring transaction type.

UpdateRecurringTransactionRequest.description:
A recurring transaction to update over REST. Same shape as CreateRecurringTransactionRequest -
there is no id field, since the route's {id} is the only source of the id, matching
BillsController.UpdateBill's existing convention.

schedule.description:
The schedule that determines when each occurrence is generated. Required unless
RecurringScheduleType is Unscheduled, in which case it is optional and,
when supplied, only its timing fields are used to compute reminders.

recurringScheduleType.description: The type of schedule for the recurring transaction. Defaults to Scheduled.

transactionType.description:
The type of transaction this template generates. Determines how Template
is interpreted.

autoSendEmail.description:
Whether each generated transaction should be automatically emailed. Only applies to
Bill and Invoice; ignored for Journal, Payment and Receipt.

sendDate.description: The date to send the email on, when AutoSendEmail is true. Only applies to Bill.

template.description:
The transaction-type-specific template. Its shape is one of five concrete types
(bill, invoice, journal, payment or receipt), selected by TransactionType.

RecurringTransactionListItem.description:
A recurring transaction template, as shown in the recurring transactions list. Generic across
all transaction types - does not include the type-specific template body (line items,
supplier/customer details, etc.); use the get-by-id endpoint for that. Backed by the same
external list service the Kendo recurring transactions grid uses, so Status and
Frequency are the display-ready strings it returns rather than structured enums;
TransactionType is parsed into the same enum POST/PUT use, for consistency.

transactionType.description:
The type of transaction this template generates. Null if the underlying list service
returns a type outside the five POST/PUT support (e.g. legacy credit note/bill credit data).

contactName.description: The name of the contact (customer or supplier) this template is for.

contactId.description:
The id of the contact (customer or supplier) this template is for. Null if the template has no contact,
e.g. a journal.

startDate.description: The date of the first occurrence.

endDate.description: The date of the last occurrence, when the schedule ends on a specific date.

frequency.description: How often each occurrence is generated.

recurringType.description:
Whether occurrences are generated on a schedule or created manually. Null if the underlying list
service returns a schedule type this API does not recognise.

nextTransactionDate.description: The date of the next occurrence.

amount.description: The transaction amount.

groupId.description: The id of the recurring transaction group the template is in. Null if it is not in a group.

groupName.description:
The name of the recurring transaction group the template is in. Null if it is not in a group, or if
recurring transaction groups are not available to the user.

RecurringTransactionDetail.description:
A recurring transaction template, including its type-specific body. Returned by the REST
get-by-id endpoint - a REST-only type, not part of the GraphQL schema (unlike the base
RecurringTransactionTemplate, which the skip/status GraphQL mutations also return).

group.description: The group the template is assigned to, or null when it is not in a group.

schedule.description:
The schedule that determines when each occurrence is generated, or null for an
unscheduled template with no reminder.

attachments.description:
The documents attached to the recurring template. Only recurring invoices have an
attachments experience, so the GraphQL schema exposes this on
RecurringInvoiceTemplate alone, via RecurringInvoiceTemplateGraphql.

recurringType.description: Recurring type of the template, which is used to determine the type of transaction that will be created from this template.

transactionType.description: The type of transaction this template generates. Determines Template's shape.

template.description:
The transaction-type-specific template. For Invoice and Journal, the same rich shape the
GraphQL recurring-transaction queries return. For Bill, Payment and Receipt, a dedicated rich
read shape (RecurringBillTemplate, RecurringPaymentTemplate,
RecurringReceiptTemplate) with every id resolved to a named reference.

RecurringTransactionGroupRef.description: Reference to the group a recurring transaction template is assigned to.

RecurringSchedule.description: The schedule of a recurring transaction.

startDate.description: The date of the first occurrence.

endCondition.description: The condition for when the schedule ends.

RecurringFrequency.description: The frequency of a recurring schedule.

value.description: The number of periods between each occurrence.

lastDayOfEachMonth.description: Whether to always use the last day of each month for each occurrence.

RecurringEndCondition.description: The end condition of a recurring schedule.

type.description: When to stop generating recurring transactions.

value.description: The end value, interpreted based on the type: null for "Never", a number of occurrences for "After", or a date for "AtDate".

TransactionActionsSummary.description: What the transaction actions on a transaction form have to offer for one contact.

actionCount.description: How many actions are available, for the actions button's label.

actions.description: The actions, in the order they are presented.

TransactionAction.description: One shortcut offered on a transaction form for populating it from data already in the book.

available.description: Whether the action has anything to offer for the contact.

count.description: How many items the action has to offer, or null for the actions shown without a number.

FrequentlyUsedDetails.description:
A page of the items and ledger accounts the contact is charged most often, ranked by how often and how
recently they were used.

rows.description: The rows on the requested page.

total.description: How many rows the search and row type filter matched, across every page.

unfilteredTotal.description:
How many rows the contact has at all, ignoring the search text and the row type filter. Zero means
the contact has nothing to offer; anything else with a total of zero means the filter matched
nothing.

FrequentlyUsedRow.description:
One item or ledger account the contact has been charged before, carrying everything needed to build a
line from it without a second call.

rowType.description: Whether the row is an item or a ledger account.

id.description: The chargeable item's or ledger account's id.

name.description: The full name, including any parent.

code.description: The item code or account code.

itemType.description:
What kind of item the row is. Null for a ledger account, which has no item type — which is also why
filtering by item type leaves ledger accounts out.

description.description: The item's sale description. Null for a ledger account.

unitPrice.description: The item's sale price. Null for a ledger account.

unitPriceAccuracy.description: How many decimal places the sale price is held to. Null for a ledger account.

unitPriceIsTaxInclusive.description: Whether the sale price includes tax. Null for a ledger account.

accountId.description: The account the line posts to — the item's sale account, or the row itself.

taxGroupId.description: The tax group the line defaults to.

taxGroupName.description: The tax group's code, which is the short name it is shown under rather than its description.

usageCount.description: How many of the contact's lines used this row within the ranking window.

lastUsedDate.description: The date of the most recent transaction that used this row.

RecentTransactionsDetails.description:
A page of the contact's recent transactions, newest first, each carrying the lines that can be
copied onto the transaction being written.

rows.description: The transactions on the requested page.

total.description: How many transactions the search and item type filter matched, across every page.

unfilteredTotal.description:
How many transactions the contact has at all, ignoring the search text and the item type
filter. Zero means the contact has nothing to offer; anything else with a total of zero means
the filter matched nothing.

RecentTransaction.description:
One of the contact's past transactions, with the lines that can be copied onto the transaction
being written.

transactionNumber.description: The number the transaction is shown under.

lines.description: The lines that can be copied, in the order they appear on the transaction.

RecentTransactionLine.description:
One line from a past transaction, carrying everything needed to put it on the transaction being
written without a second call.

rowType.description:
Whether the line is for an item or a ledger account. The same row type the frequently used
rows carry, so the two actions insert through one path.

id.description: The chargeable item's or ledger account's id.

lineNumber.description:
Where the line sits on the transaction, which is also what tells two lines for the same item
apart. Unique within a transaction, so the transaction's id and this number key the line.

name.description: The item's or ledger account's full name, including any parent.

code.description: The item code or account code.

itemType.description:
What kind of item the line is for. Null for a ledger account line, which is also why filtering
by item type leaves ledger account lines out.

description.description: The description as it was written on the line.

quantity.description: The quantity as it was charged.

unitPrice.description: The unit price as it was charged.

unitPriceAccuracy.description: How many decimal places the unit price was held to.

unitPriceIsTaxInclusive.description: Whether the unit price included tax.

amount.description:
What the line came to. This is where a ledger account line holds its value, since an account
line is entered as an amount rather than a price and a quantity.

discountAmount.description: The discount taken off the line as a value.

discountPercent.description: The discount taken off the line as a percentage.

taxAmount.description: The tax charged on the line.

taxIsModified.description:
Whether the tax was overridden rather than calculated, so a copy keeps the tax that was
actually charged instead of silently recalculating it.

accountId.description: The account the line posts to — the item's sale account, or the line's own account.

taxGroupId.description: The tax group the line was charged under.

taxGroupName.description: The tax group's code, which is the short name it is shown under rather than its description.

roles.description: List of roles user is assigned to.

currentUser.description: Indicates whether this is the currently logged in user.

lastLoggedInDateTime.description: The last time the user logged in.

UserRoles.description: A list of roles the user is assigned to.

roles.description: A list of roles the user is assigned to.
